rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the accusation that others came from the right, this means from the religion: they tempted people away from faith and made religion seem doubtful.
rows.anchor: أي من قبل الدين أي تفتنوننا عن الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the right are the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وأصحاب اليمين ما أصحاب اليمين يعني أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yamin can mean the right-hand side; the right-side groups are arranged in circles, and Moses was called from the right side of the mountain.
rows.anchor: يعني جانب اليمين حلقا حلقا

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes interpret taking him by the right as taking him by the truth and proof.
rows.anchor: لأخذنا منه باليمين يعني بالحق والحجة على قول بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm can mean one of the six days in which God created the world.
rows.anchor: يوم يعني من الأيام الستة التي خلق الله تعالى فيها الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm can mean a day of worldly time; the cited day is measured by the descent of Gabriel and equals a thousand years by human reckoning.
rows.anchor: يوم يعني يوما من أيام الدنيا قوله تعالى في سورة السجدة يدبر الأمر من السماء إلى الأرض ثم يعرج اليه في يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm can mean the Day of Resurrection, as in the sealing of mouths, the people of Paradise being occupied, the scales, and each soul's recompense.
rows.anchor: اليوم نختم على أفواههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm can mean a time or occasion, as in the times of birth, death, resurrection, travel, residence, and harvest.
rows.anchor: وسلام عليه يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا يعني حين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm can mean the day the Romans defeat Persia; another reported identification is the day of Hudaybiyyah.
rows.anchor: ويومئذ يفرح المؤمنون بنصر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm can mean the day the sun rises from the west.
rows.anchor: يوم يأتي بعض آيات ربك يعني يوم طلوع الشمس من مغربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ means equal or the same, glossed by the verb yastawī.
rows.anchor: أي ( يستوي ) قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah means a portion or chapter of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: السورة القطعة من القرآن السور بغير هاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūr means a barrier; here it is the separating wall whose inner side is mercy and which the source identifies with al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: السور الحاجز قوله تعالى في سورة الحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase about uncovering a ساق, sāq means hardship or distress.
rows.anchor: الساق الشدة قوله تعالى في سورة القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāq can mean the actual leg; its plural is sūq, as in the horses' legs.
rows.anchor: الساق بعينها جمعها سوق قوله تعالى في سورة ص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawiyy can mean sound and free from illness; Maryam's sign means no muteness or other affliction.
rows.anchor: السوي يعني الصحيح من الداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawiyy can describe a well-formed human figure; the related forms also mean that God fashioned a creature's form.
rows.anchor: السوي في الخلقة وصورة البشر قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawiyy can mean just or upright; the person walking evenly on a straight path is guided justly.
rows.anchor: السوي العدل قوله تعالى في سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istawā ilā means to intend or turn toward, as God turns toward the heaven.
rows.anchor: استوى بمعنى قصد وعمد قوله تعالى في سورة فصلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istawā can mean to settle; the ark settled on Mount Judi.
rows.anchor: استوى بمعنى استقر قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istawā can mean to ride or board, as when people ride a conveyance or a ship.
rows.anchor: استوى أي ركب قوله تعالى في سورة الزخرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istawā can mean to become strong and mature; the source explains the phrase as the completion of one's form at forty years.
rows.anchor: استوى بمعنى قوي واشتد قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qarin in this passage is the Satan paired with a human in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: الثالث القرين الشيطان المقرون بابن آدم في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarana can describe people yoked or joined together in a single chain.
rows.anchor: يقرنان في سلسلة واحدة كقوله تعالى في سورة إبراهيم مقرنين في الأصفاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moqrinin can mean owners or those able to control something.
rows.anchor: المقرن أي المالك قوله تعالى في سورة الزخرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿmah can mean God's favor or blessing bestowed on people.
rows.anchor: عليكم أي منته مثلها في سورة الأحزاب والمائدة كقوله تعالى في سورة البقرة يا بني اسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿmah can mean God's religion and Book; changing it is abandoning the religion, and the believers' unity is through Islam.
rows.anchor: الثاني النعمة دين الله وكتابه قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The niʿmah that people recognize and then deny is Muhammad; the source also cites denial of God's blessings.
rows.anchor: الثالث النعمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿmah can mean God's reward.
rows.anchor: الرابع النعمة الثواب قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿmah can refer to kingship and wealth.
rows.anchor: الخامس النعمة الملك والغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿmah can mean prophethood, as in the people favored with prophecy.
rows.anchor: السادس النعمة النبوة قوله تعالى في فاتحة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿmah can mean God's mercy.
rows.anchor: السابع النعمة الرحمة قوله سبحانه في الحجرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿmah can mean God's beneficence, for which no person owes repayment.
rows.anchor: الثامن النعمة الإحسان من الله قوله تعالى في سورة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naʿʿamahu means God expanded a person's livelihood; the source compares God's abundant blessings.
rows.anchor: التاسع النعمة سعة العيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one God favored and the Prophet favored by freeing him is Zayd ibn Harithah: God favored him with Islam and the Prophet manumitted him.
rows.anchor: العاشر المنعم عليه المعتق قوله سبحانه في سورة الأحزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nufūs here means hearts; the source likewise glosses Joseph's reference to his own nafs as his heart.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها النفس القلب قوله تعالى في سورة النجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sariyy means a small river or stream, glossed as a small channel.
rows.anchor: السري النهر الصغير قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree from which Moses was called is identified as a boxthorn.
rows.anchor: الشجرة يعني العوسج قوله سبحانه في سورة القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree Adam and his wife were forbidden to approach is identified as a grapevine.
rows.anchor: الشجرة الكرم قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree growing on Mount Sinai and the blessed tree supplying oil are identified as the olive.
rows.anchor: الشجرة الزيتون قوله تعالى في سورة المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree growing from the base of Hell and the cursed tree are the tree of Zaqqum.
rows.anchor: الشجرة يعني شجرة الزقوم قوله تعالى في سورة الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good tree in the parable of the good word is identified as a palm tree.
rows.anchor: الشجرة النخلة قوله تعالى في سورة إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree beneath which the believers pledged allegiance is identified as the sidr tree.
rows.anchor: الشجرة يعني السمرة قوله تعالى في سورة الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant God caused to grow over Jonah is identified as a gourd.
rows.anchor: الشجرة يعني شجرة القرع قوله تعالى في صورة الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajar here means every tree that has a trunk.
rows.anchor: الشجرة كل شجرة لها ساق قوله تعالى في سورة الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil tree uprooted from the earth is identified as the colocynth.
rows.anchor: الشجرة شجرة الحنظل قوله تعالى في سورة إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashadd can mean more enduring, as in greater love for God and return to a more intense punishment.
rows.anchor: أشد يعني أدوم قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashadd can mean harsher or more severe toward the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أشد أغلظ قوله تعالى في سورة الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashadd can mean worse or more evil, as in the source's comparison of persecution with killing.
rows.anchor: أشد يعني أكثر شرا قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashadd can mean stronger in power.
rows.anchor: أشد أقوى قوله تعالى في سورة حم السجدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashadd can mean more hostile, as in the source's description of Jews and idolaters as most hostile to believers.
rows.anchor: أشد يعني أعدى قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: غريب القرآن
rows.claim: Al-najm means plants: what sprouts from the earth without a trunk; the cited source contrasts this with trees that have trunks.
rows.anchor: النجم ما نجم من الأرض أي طلع ولم يكن على ساق كالعشب والبقل والشجر ما قام على ساق قال في غريب القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najāt can mean rescue and release from punishment, as in God's rescue of the Israelites from Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : النجاة والخلاص من العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najāt can mean safety from destruction, as in the rescue of Moses and his companions and the saving of messengers and believers.
rows.anchor: الثاني النجاة السلامة من الهلاك قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najwah is a raised bank or shore; Pharaoh's body is cast there at the edge of the sea.
rows.anchor: ثالثا النجوة من النجاة قوله تعالى في سورة يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najāt can mean monotheism, the salvation to which the speaker calls his people.
rows.anchor: الرابع النجاة التوحيد قوله تعالى في سورة غافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nidāʾ can mean the call to prayer, the adhān.
rows.anchor: النداء الاذان قوله سبحانه في سورة الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ithm means disobedience or sinful acts; the source illustrates this with forbidden conduct and the ban on cooperating in sin.
rows.anchor: الإثم يعني المعصية فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source also reports that ithm can mean wine.
rows.anchor: يعني المعاصي ويقال الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ithm can mean liability or sin; in this verse, having no sin means the person's sin is forgiven.
rows.anchor: الإثم والذنب قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil specifically interprets ithm here as an error, particularly in the context of punishment.
rows.anchor: الإثم يعني الخطأ قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajr can mean a dowry.
rows.anchor: الأجر بمعنى المهر قوله تعالى في سورة الأحزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajr can mean the reward for obedience; the source also glosses the Prophet's reward as thawāb.
rows.anchor: الأجر الثواب على الطاعة قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajr can mean a payment or fee, as in a payment offered for service; the source also cites asking no fee and payment for watering.
rows.anchor: الأجر الجعل فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة سبأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajr can mean maintenance or expenses owed to a nursing mother.
rows.anchor: الأجر النفقة . فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة الطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajal can mean death; God does not defer a soul once its death has arrived.
rows.anchor: الأجل بمعنى الموت قال الله عز وجل في سورة المنافقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amr can mean a command, as in God's commands to justice and to return trusts to their owners.
rows.anchor: الأمر بعينه . قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amr can mean a sin and its consequence or punishment.
rows.anchor: الأمر يعني الذنب . قوله تعالى في سورة الطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amr can mean victory; the source also glosses God's amr in the Romans passage as victory.
rows.anchor: الأمر يعني النصر . قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amr can mean affairs or matters, as in the affairs returning to God and Pharaoh's affair not being right-guided.
rows.anchor: الأمر الفعل والشأن , كقوله تعالى في سورة الشورى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse about there being no refuge from God's amr, amr means drowning.
rows.anchor: الأمر يعني الغرق . قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light, doubled, and lengthened readings of amarnā are described as meaning We increased the town's affluent people; the doubled form may instead mean We empowered its tyrants or made them rulers.
rows.anchor: امرنا ( بالتخفيف ) وامرنا ( بتشديد الميم ) وآمرنا ( بالمد ) أكثرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imr, with kasrah, means an abominable or objectionable thing.
rows.anchor: المنكر , قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry lists five senses of umm: origin, destination, biological mother, wet nurse, and the Prophet's wives.
rows.anchor: الأصل . المرجع . الوالدة بعينها . المرضع . أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm can mean origin: the Mother of the Book is its source, and Umm al-Qurā is the origin of towns.
rows.anchor: الأم أي الأصل . قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm can mean a person's return and destination.
rows.anchor: الأم المرجع والمصير . قوله تعالى في سورة القارعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm can mean one's biological mother, as in Moses being returned to his mother.
rows.anchor: الأم الوالدة بعينها . قوله تعالى في سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting God's Book behind one's back means they did not honor or act on it and instead practiced sorcery.
rows.anchor: كتاب الله وراء ظهورهم يعني جعلوا كتاب الله تعالى يظهر ولا يعظمونه ولا يعملون به بل عملوا بالسحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓahīrah means midday, when people pray the noon prayer; it also means the midday period when people set aside their clothes.
rows.anchor: الظهيرة نصف النهار قوله تعالى في سورة الروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIbādah can mean worshipping God alone or affirming His oneness.
rows.anchor: اعبدوا يعني وحدوا قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIbādah can mean obedience; the source glosses those worshipped as those obeyed and says not to obey Satan.
rows.anchor: اعبدوا بمعنى اطبعوا قوله تعالى في سورة سبأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIbād can mean slaves or servants, as in God's servants, the servants attributed to God, and household slaves.
rows.anchor: العباد المماليك قوله تعالى في سورة الزمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjaban can mean despairing, as the source glosses the fish episode.
rows.anchor: عجبا اي يائسا قوله سبحانه في سورة الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjab can mean astonishment, as in the reactions of the disbelievers and the astonishment at their statement.
rows.anchor: العجب الاستعظام كقوله سبحانه في سورة الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjaban can mean noble or honorable; the jinn describe the Qur'an as noble and distinguished.
rows.anchor: عجبا اي كريما قوله تعالى في سورة الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʿjizūn means those who might outrun or escape God, which the source says they cannot do.
rows.anchor: معجزون سابقون قوله سبحانه في سورة العنكبوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʿājizūn means those who hinder or try to thwart others.
rows.anchor: الثاني معاجزون مثبطون قوله تعالى في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhn can mean God's command, including the command by which signs are given and messengers are obeyed.
rows.anchor: الإذن بمعنى الأمر قوله تعالى في سورة الرعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhā can mean something forbidden; the source glosses menstruation as forbidden.
rows.anchor: الأذى يعني الحرام . قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhā can mean lice on the head.
rows.anchor: الأذى يعني القمل . قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhā can mean hardship caused by rain.
rows.anchor: الأذى الشدة . قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhā can mean insulting or reproaching someone; the source connects this gloss with hearing much abuse from earlier scripture communities and polytheists.
rows.anchor: الأذى يعنى الشم . قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source says this ruling was abrogated by the hundred lashes.
rows.anchor: وقد نسخ السبب مجلد مائة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhā can mean slander: God cleared Moses of what people said about him, including the allegation that he was physically defective.
rows.anchor: الأذى البهتان قوله تعالى في سورة الأحزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhā can mean disobedience; the source identifies the people who harm God and His Messenger here as Jews who disobey God.
rows.anchor: الأذى العصيان . قوله تعالى في سورة الأحزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhā can mean staying behind; the source interprets this phrase as those who stayed behind from the Tabuk expedition.
rows.anchor: الأذى التخلف . قوله تعالى في سورة التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghy can mean disobedience or transgression; the source says the harm of people's transgression returns to themselves.
rows.anchor: البغي يعني المعصية . قوله تعالى في سورة يس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghy can mean envy, as in envy that God sent down His bounty and division after knowledge came.
rows.anchor: البغي الحسد . قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghy can mean fornication; the source applies the sense to Mary's denial and to the prohibition on forcing women into prostitution.
rows.anchor: البغاء الزنا . قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqiyyah can mean God's reward.
rows.anchor: البقية بمعنى الثواب قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-bāqiyāt al-ṣāliḥāt can mean the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: البقية الصلوات الخمس . قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف ومريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqiyyah can mean what remains from something that has gone; the source also cites a word made enduring among Abraham's descendants.
rows.anchor: البقية الباقي من الذاهب . قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāqī can mean lasting or enduring, as in what remains with God and what is better and more lasting.
rows.anchor: البقاء الدوام . قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqiyyah can mean a small number of people.
rows.anchor: البقية يعني القلة . قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balad has four senses in this entry: Mecca, Saba, fertile land, and a saline barren place; the cited examples identify the blessed and secure land as Mecca.
rows.anchor: مكة . سبأ . البقعة النامية . مكان سبخ لا نبات فيه
